items.summary: NetLink NBN Trust named former ST Engineering and Singtel executive Low Ka Hoe as its CEO-designate, succeeding Tong Yew Heng effective Nov 10. A bourse filing dated Nov 6 states he will take over on Apr 1, 2027, when he also joins the manager's board as an executive director. The trustee-manager added that NetLink posted a distribution per unit of $0.0274 for its first half ended Sep 30, up 1.1% from a year earlier; units closed flat at $0.94 on Friday. Derryn Wong reported the item in THE BUSINESS TIMES.
items.title: Low Ka Hoe Named NetLink NBN Trust CEO-Successor

items.summary: Schroders is selling Wisteria Mall in Yishun, northern Singapore, through brokers Knight Frank and Savills to raise around $220 million. The exercise closes late November. Schroders acquired the London-based asset manager by Nuveen in October and bought the mall for $208 million in 2022; it is now about 93% occupied. A spokesperson said the firm regularly reviews its real estate portfolios to serve investors.
items.title: Schroders Lists Singapore Mall in Property Offload Push

items.summary: The author spent two years comparing manual heating control with an AI system, Tado X, in a 1930s solid-brick house. After controlling for hot water usage across the same 213 days from November to May and similar outside temperatures, the AI-controlled heating used 11,735.7 kWh of gas versus 14,316.7 kWh manually — a reduction of about 18%, or 2,581 kWh less. At the current energy price cap ending 31 December, that equates to £205.70 saved. The author notes savings could be larger for less frugal households and highlights comfort benefits beyond efficiency.
items.title: A Two-Year Test of AI Heating Controls

items.summary: A survey invites school leaders, teachers, and parents to describe their experiences with artificial intelligence tools in communication between families and schools. It asks respondents whether they have received or written AI-generated emails, what impact those messages had on tone and quality, and whether the technology has eased contact or created new problems. The request notes that people having trouble completing the form can click a link for help.
items.title: Schools and parents invited to share AI email experiences

items.summary: The IEA’s India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026, launched at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit in New Delhi, expects India’s installed solar PV capacity to exceed 350 GW by 2030. Total renewable power could reach around 530 GW, with wind near 90 GW and hydropower at 75 GW. The path includes rooftop schemes like PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and corporate procurement; sustained expansion would need faster grid, storage and flexibility investment.
items.title: IEA Forecasts India Solar Capacity Surpassing 350 GW by 2030

items.summary: A research team from Soochow University in China developed a portable solar-powered device that produces drinking water from turbid, saline, oily and highly acidic sources. The prototype produced 1. 64 liters of clean water in eight hours using an evaporation surface measuring just 30. 72 cm². It combines foldable solar cells with a Fresnel lens to concentrate sunlight onto the surface without grid or fuel supply. Outdoor tests were conducted on selected days in January and February 2025, achieving apparent energy efficiency of 93. 31% and production rate of 69. 46 liters per square meter per hour.
items.title: Soochow University Team Unveils Portable Solar Watermaker

items.summary: Nationwide building society launched a fixed-rate Member Exclusive Bond paying 5.3% interest, available to its more than 19 million members with deposits of £1 to £10,000. A full £10,000 deposit earns £1,381 over the 30-month term. The launch follows a Bank of England base rate rise to 4%. Nationwide says it rewards member loyalty; experts expect fixed rates to hold after Thursday's hike.
items.title: Nationwide Launches Fixed-Rate Savings Account at Market-Leading Rate

items.summary: Environmental groups worldwide are turning to artificial intelligence to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife – embracing a technology they also warn is driving surges in electricity demand, water use and greenhouse-gas emissions. The contradiction forces these organizations to justify their AI use while fighting the crises it worsens. Groups like Conservation International say AI helps them move faster amid urgent biodiversity threats; Kenya's Save the Elephants cut survey time from nine months to hours. Data-center footprint could more than double by 2030, and global consumption is projected at about 945 terawatt-hours annually – roughly equal to Japan's use. Organizations like Greenpeace push back on new data centers as unnecessary.
items.title: Environmental Groups Adopt AI While Warning of Its Environmental Costs

items.summary: Rakesh Shah of Edelweiss urged the government in a Bloomberg Television interview to consider removing capital gains tax to attract foreign investors. Foreign outflows exceeded $28 billion this year, yet inflows topped $5 billion over three weeks amid domestic recovery. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said she would look at market-related tax changes without confirming specifics.
items.title: Edelweiss Chairman Calls for Scrapping Capital Gains Tax

items.summary: A London-based commentator weighs in on repeated tech-stock shakeouts, asking whether the AI bubble is finally bursting or just another head fake. He notes that AI assets dominate markets and show hallmarks of an unsustainable boom, citing Bank for International Settlements figures that nearly 29 per cent of AI firms’ investment deals are with other AI firms. Markets briefly rose after Democratic midterm wins but fell sharply when voters rejected data centres; the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5 per cent on Thursday (Nov 5), its biggest fall in 19 months, while CoreWeave stocks fell 10 per cent and Sandisk 22 per cent. Trevor Greetham of Royal London Asset Management called the AI trade a shark that must keep swimming to stay alive.
items.title: Commentator Questions Whether AI Stock Bubble Is Bursting

items.summary: CGTN Digital journalist Shen Shiwei interviewed CEOs from the US, Germany and Switzerland, plus a Moldovan official, about their selections at the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The leaders highlighted products prioritizing innovation, high technology, low carbon output, eco-friendliness and user orientation, with China's 15th Five-Year Plan among the topics of focus.
items.title: Global CEOs Share Top Picks at CIIE

items.summary: China delivered its latest financial work report, presented by central bank Governor Pan Gongsheng to the NPC Standing Committee. The report shows local government financing vehicle debt fell 92% from March 2023 levels, with operational debt down 79%, and approved over 8.4 trillion yuan of real estate loans. Deputies flagged lingering risks while calling for market stabilization measures and deeper opening-up. New corporate loan rates reached a historic low of 2.96%. The report sets five priorities centered on supportive monetary policy and no systemic risk.
items.title: NPC Deputies Urge Market Stability and Financial Opening-Up in China's Work Report

items.summary: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries promises to stop tariffs raising American prices, while incoming Senate Finance Committee chairman Ron Wyden says he will reassert congressional authority over trade policy. Even Republican Senator Ted Cruz called tariffs too expensive. Lawmakers warn curbing President Donald Trump's tariff powers may be difficult and could trigger infighting in both parties as new duties loom.
items.title: Democrats Vow to Challenge Trump Tariffs Over Rising Costs

items.summary: In Nelson, Blair Cameron leads by 878 votes with 72% of the vote counted, a margin under 1000 still seen as tight. Winston Peters urged calm until all facts are known. Projected seat counts show National at 42 and Labour at 35 in a shifting parliament.
items.title: NZ Election Count Tight in Nelson as Labour Levels With National

items.summary: A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in the UK said China strongly opposed a joint statement from the UK, United States, Canada and Australia commenting on anti-China figure Joshua Wong Chi-fung's sentencing by the Hong Kong High Court. The remarks were described as unwarranted interference in Hong Kong affairs. Beijing urged the UK to stop interfering under any pretext.
items.title: China Condemns UK and Allies Over Joshua Wong Sentencing Remarks

items.summary: A Beijing laboratory reports that DREADDs, a neurostimulation method previously used only on animals, reduced seizures by an average of 92.6% in three drug-resistant epilepsy patients (s4). The approach uses a genetically-engineered virus to alter brain receptors and clozapine to switch targeted regions off (s5-s6), with adverse events rated mild-to-moderate (grade 1 or 2) (s6). At the NIH BRAIN Initiative meeting in Bethesda, inventor Professor Brian Roth noted at least seven registered Chinese DREADDs trials (s8). Cambridge's Ewan St John-Smith called it exciting but questioned readiness and flagged viral-delivery risks (s10-s22), while others see China reshaping neuroscience leadership (s26-s30)
items.title: China Reports Early Success in Human DREADDs Trials for Epilepsy

items.summary: Santos FC announced on Friday that it has appointed Neymar's father and agent, Neymar Sr., as its chief executive. His agency NR Sports holds the rights to his son's name and image, and he reportedly played a key role in Neymar's career. According to Brazilian media reports, his contract runs until December and depends on president Marcelo Teixeira being re-elected next month.
items.title: Neymar Sr Appointed CEO of Santos FC

items.summary: Early release prisoners in England and Wales risk being released into street homelessness as temporary probation accommodation expires, according to charities and probation staff. James, a 37-year-old released from prison in August with two electronic tags, said he has nowhere to go after his Somerset housing was rejected. Tania Bassett of Napo called it a
items.title: Probation staff warn early releases face street homelessness

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV, aged 71 and three weeks post lung-cancer surgery, told reporters he is “in pretty good health” as his 12-day tour began in Montevideo, Uruguay. He praised the medical staff and said doctors report the cancer has not spread. On arrival crowds greeted him; later he urged universal healthcare to be accessible to everyone.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV opens Latin America tour in good health

items.summary: France faces mounting debt costs amid nationwide protests and a government lacking parliamentary majority. Public debt stands at around 120% of GDP, roughly double Germany's ~65%, while France carries negative credit outlooks and pays nearly 1.6 percentage points more in interest on 10-year bonds than Berlin. The spread over German bonds has doubled since June 2026. Economist Friedrich Heinemann warns rising spreads could trigger a financial crisis unless course changes occur. Researchers note many citizens remain insulated from debt consequences, sustaining political support for costly promises from both far-right and far-left parties.
items.title: France's Rising Debt Costs Threaten Stability Amid Protests

items.summary: Moscow carried out missile strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight Friday to Saturday, targeting energy infrastructure and killing at least one person while injuring eight, authorities said. Russian forces launched attacks damaging a major bridge across the Dnipro River, with explosions rocking the city as ballistic missiles hit the Northern Bridge.
items.title: Russia strikes Kyiv and surrounding region in massive overnight strike

items.summary: Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, six-year-old pandas from China's Chengdu, made their first public appearance at Zoo Atlanta on Friday as visitors queued to see them. The pair arrived September 27 after a decades-long loan arrangement ended amid strained US-China ties. Their return follows a renewed 10-year agreement following a Washington summit between President Trump and Xi Jinping.
items.title: Two Giant Pandas Make Public Debut at Zoo Atlanta

items.summary: Early results from New Zealand's general election show a neck-and-neck race between the Labour Party and National Party-led right-wing coalition after a campaign centred on cost of living. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon faces main challenger Chris Hipkins as polls close. Labour leads at 29.71% versus National's 29.41%, with just over 42% counted, though none are expected to secure a parliamentary majority.
items.title: New Zealand Counting Votes in a Close Election

items.summary: Lupovis, a cybersecurity firm led by CEO Xavier Bellekens, says it detected hackers probing internet-connected refrigeration systems across Europe in the days before supermarket and blood bank cyberattacks on 2 and 3 November. The company observed over 276 attempts from 91 threat actors targeting Danfoss’s AK-SM system manager during a 10-day reconnaissance period peaking on 26 October, suggesting a coordinated operation rather than a lone actor. Lupovis declined to confirm Russia as the culprit, noting servers’ locations do not prove nationality. Experts warn similar weaknesses could affect heating, access control and other building systems, though no ransom or claim of responsibility has emerged.
items.title: Cybersecurity firm traces fridge probes ahead of European attacks

items.summary: CNA reported that SMRT is trialling a new escalator etiquette at City Hall and Raffles Place MRT stations, encouraging commuters to stand on both sides instead of keeping left. Observations found walking up the right side took about 20 seconds versus about 30 seconds for standing still on the left, yet most passengers kept old habits. SMRT Trains president Lam Sheau Kai said the month-long trial aims to improve safety and capacity. Interviews with 10 commuters showed strong attachment to keeping left, though some acknowledged exceptions for elderly or less steady riders. Similar moves in London reportedly increased capacity by about 30 per cent, while South Korean studies cited higher wear on one side of escalators.
items.title: Singapore Commuters Resist Escalator Stand-BOTH-Sides Trial

items.summary: Stacey Waaka scored three tries as New Zealand beat Fetu Samoa in the women's Rugby League World Cup semifinal, reaching a seventh consecutive decider. The win capped her tournament of six tries and made New Zealand the only nation to reach every final since 2000. Waaka said: 'I can't wait for this next week.'
items.title: Waaka hat-trick sends Kiwi Ferns to seventh straight women's Rugby League World Cup final

items.summary: The Israeli army arrested six Palestinians early Saturday during raids across the occupied West Bank, which included home searches, according to local sources. Forces detained five people in Jenin and took them to an undisclosed location; Wafa reported a raid on Askar refugee camp near Nablus that led to one arrest. No arrests were reported in al-Zawiya, Tammun, Iktaba or al-Amari. The army conducts near-daily campaigns targeting men, women and children, often involving assaults and the destruction of household belongings. Around 9,350 Palestinian prisoners are held in Israeli prisons.
items.title: Israeli army raids West Bank, arrests six Palestinians

items.summary: South Australian Police arrested and charged a man with alleged stalking and harassment of the state's lower house Speaker, Nat Cook. The man has been bailed and is scheduled to appear in Christies Beach Magistrates Court on December 7.
items.title: Man Charged With Harassing South Australian Speaker Nat Cook

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN that a 'big agreement' voiced by US President Donald Trump to end the Russia-Ukraine war could be dangerous. Published on 07 November 2026, his comments followed Trump's Thursday confirmation of talks with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev. Zelenskyy said he saw no signals from Moscow and compared any settlement to Yalta, warning Ukraine should not be divided by Russia.
items.title: Zelenskyy Warns Trump's Proposed Deal Could Be Dangerous

items.summary: Mogadishu residents reacted with mixed feelings after Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on Friday that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension was unlawful. The opposition accuses the president of deploying troops to arrest the court's chief justice, claims AFP could not verify but which Somali media images reportedly support. The ruling follows disputes over constitutional amendments and comes amid a security crisis linked to Al-Shabaab as international donors cut funding.
items.title: Somalia Supreme Court ruling sparks political crisis over president's term extension

items.summary: Tokyo is considering paying its 2027 contributions to the International Criminal Court ahead of schedule, government sources said, in response to U.S. sanctions on the court. A Japanese official warned Friday that without action the ICC could face a funding shortfall. The ICC's 2026 budget totals about €196 million, or about ¥34.5 billion, and Japan contributed about ¥4.6 billion this year as its largest donor. Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Thursday Tokyo would consider financial measures while communicating with President Tomoko Akane.
items.title: Japan Weighs Early ICC Contribution Amid U.S. Sanctions

items.summary: Juan Manuel Santos, former president of Colombia (2010-2018), is the subject of an EL PAÍS profile built from four interviews conducted between April and September 2025. The piece opens with his January 2025 appearance before the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, where he watched the Doomsday Clock sit at 89 seconds to midnight in 2025 and move closer — to 85 seconds away — by January 2026. Santos frames himself as a lifelong negotiator whose career moved from defense minister under Álvaro Uribe (2006-2009) to architect of the peace agreement with the FARC, signed in 2016 after more than 50 years of war. Ten years later he marks that anniversary while acknowledging its non-implementation and today's gang-driven violence. He attributes current global conflict partly to lost moderation and social media polarization, yet insists conflicts remain solvable: 'It's simply a matter of sitting down and talking.' The interviews were shaped by the June 2025 election victory and swearing-in of Abelardo de la Espriella, whose display of corpses after a military operation prompted Santos to reflect on state legitimacy. Attribution throughout carries uncertainty — many claims are his own interpretations rather than verified fact — while figures like the clock's setting remain stated flatly by the Bulletin.
items.title: Former Colombian President Reflects on Peace and a Fraying World

items.summary: Human rights activist and 2023 Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi, interviewed by EL PAÍS from a Tehran prison video room while awaiting an 18-year sentence suspended in May after two heart attacks, describes the prize as having intensified pressure on her. She recounts being detained at least 14 times and tried 10 times, accumulating 44 years’ imprisonment and 154 lashes plus 161 days of solitary confinement since writing her memoir from Evin prison. Calling isolation “one of the Islamic Republic’s main instruments of torture,” she links it to coerced confessions and rising executions—citing Amnesty International’s estimate that around 4,500 people were executed in Iran alone during summer 1988—and credits women-led movements for advancing rights at high cost. She warns war with Israel and the United States has made the regime more repressive while she continues to hope to see her twins again one day.
items.title: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi defends Iran’s resistance amid renewed repression

items.summary: Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader, a 23-year-old Somali woman, guides visitors to Jazeera beach, sand dunes, the fish market and historic sites in an effort to reshape how the world sees Mogadishu. She works alongside her father, who guided for over three decades, and reaches wider audiences through TikTok videos of her tours. Sucdi says many tourists arrive expecting insecurity but are surprised by the country's beauty and welcoming people. Somalia's tourism department reported about 10,000 tourists visited in 2024, a 50% increase on the previous year, though she notes numbers remain low with five visitors a week considered success. Sucdi says her goal is to show landscapes, culture and people beyond negative headlines.
items.title: Somali tour guide reimagines Mogadishu beyond its headlines

items.summary: Officials across Europe reported a fresh wave of bomb threats against multiple flights on Friday, November 6, following a string of hoaxes that caused flight diversions this week. The threats may be spreading beyond aviation: two broadcasters also received security warnings. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi covered the developing situation.
items.title: European Aviation Disrupted by Fresh Bomb Threats on Friday

items.summary: According to a US intelligence memo cited by the Financial Times, American officials believe Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (Huang Le), an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed suspected of spying for China. The findings predate Trump's Beijing summit and follow New York Times reporting on surveillance linking her to information passing to Beijing amid chip-export scrutiny. Nvidia declined to comment, while the company said it had already debunked smuggling claims; China dismissed the accusations as groundless smears.
items.title: US Intelligence Memo Alleges Nvidia CEO's Romantic Ties to Chinese Spy

items.summary: A Financial Times report citing unnamed officials says a US intelligence memo from early 2026 alleged that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, suspected of working for China's Ministry of State Security. The claims follow earlier reporting on surveillance and photos. Nvidia called the interactions routine business meetings; China dismissed them as groundless speculation. No public charges exist against either person.
items.title: Nvidia, China and US Officials Reject Alleged Spy Operation Tied to Jensen Huang

items.summary: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of disrupting traditional Kali Puja celebrations after an alleged attack on Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's residence. In a statement, she asked why attackers came at 3:00 in the morning with a gang of thugs if they had the courage to use a bulldozer. Abhishek claimed the incident followed reconnaissance and called it his seventh attempt on his life.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee Condemns Attack on Abhishek Banerjee Ahead of Kali Puja

items.summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge accused the Central government of misleading people about ethanol content in E20 petrol, citing NABL-accredited laboratory reports he said showed blending up to 35-40 per cent against announced limits. He alleged the programme benefits companies linked to Union ministers and called it an experiment on India's population. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi separately claimed samples from seven Karnataka districts exceeded 20 per cent ethanol. State-run oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL disputed both findings, saying their fuel meets IS 17021 specifications of 19-21 per cent and questioning the sampling procedures.
items.title: Karnataka minister alleges Centre is over-blending ethanol in E20 petrol

items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India recorded its highest-ever Electronic Gold Receipts trading volume, with festive-period activity reaching 2,27,692 units according to the exchange. NSE Chief Business Development Officer Sriram Krishnan said the record reflects growing acceptance of regulated gold ownership and could help mobilise domestic recycled gold while potentially reducing import dependence.
items.title: NSE EGR Trading Hits Record on Dhanteras

items.summary: Seven experts offered views on buying gold and silver ahead of the festival, warning that near-term volatility, rising interest rates and inflation could pressure prices. Abhisek Bahinipati of Invesco Mutual Fund suggested a 15% allocation to precious metals for most investors, with roughly two-thirds in gold and one-third in silver. Others cautioned against chasing recent gains or deploying full amounts at once, favouring staggered buying. Motilal Oswal Private Wealth kept its outlook neutral amid higher yields, while Nuvama flagged that sharp corrections could redirect liquidity toward equities.
items.title: Experts weigh in on gold and silver investing this Diwali

items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India detailed changes in two circulars issued on November 6, covering the closing price discovery mechanism for eligible equity securities, derivatives trading hours and futures settlement prices. The revisions follow a Securities and Exchange Board of India circular dated October 15, 2026. Most provisions take effect from December 7, 2026, while changes to unexecuted limit and disclosed quantity orders begin February 8, 2027.
items.title: NSE Overhauls Closing Price Discovery and Derivatives Rules from December

items.summary: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has invited applications from DPIIT-registered startups in film and allied technologies to participate in the WaveX Startup Pavilion at WAVES Bazaar during the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) Goa 2026, which will be held from November 20 to 28. The initiative aims to give innovative startups a platform to showcase products, technologies and solutions to national and international film and media industry participants while enabling networking with filmmakers, production houses and investors. Eligible applicants are screened by a Selection Committee constituted by WaveX, the Ministry's startup accelerator for the Media and Entertainment sector.
items.title: I&B Ministry Opens Startup Applications for WAVES Bazaar Film Pavilion at IFFI Goa 2026

items.summary: Over the five trading sessions ending November 6, the Sensex rose 8.82%, or 6,568 points, to close at 81,028, gaining each session. Amid this broad-based rally, around 45 stocks from the BSE 200 index advanced in all five consecutive sessions from November 2 to 6. From these, nine were shortlisted for consistent gains throughout the period, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 15% to 20%. Data source: ACE Equity.
items.title: Nine Stocks Gained for Five Days in a Row on Sensex Rally

items.summary: Stock exchanges BSE and NSE are set to hold the Muhurat Trading session from 2.20 pm to 3.30 pm on Sunday, marking an age-old Diwali tradition tied to Lakshmi Puja and the start of Samvat 2083. The one-hour session follows a week in which Sensex surged 6,569 points while Nifty rallied nearly 9%, adding about Rs 29 lakh crore to BSE market capitalisation above Rs 500 lakh crore. Analysts advise selective, quality-first investing rather than chasing momentum, noting the limited participation of such sessions. SBI Securities outlines technical levels for Nifty around 24,830-24,850 support and 25,150-25,180 resistance.
items.title: BSE and NSE Set for Muhurat Trading Session on Sunday

items.summary: The Gurugram district administration issued show-cause notices to private commercial establishments, including the law firms Trilegal and JSA Advocates & Solicitors on Golf Course Road, after inspections found them exceeding a 50% physical office attendance limit. The mandate was set by Deputy Commissioner Uttam Singh following directions from the Commission for Air Quality Management amid worsening air quality in Delhi-NCR between 5 and 20 November. Inspections reportedly showed JSA with around 87 of 117 employees present, against a permitted limit of about 58, and Trilegal with around 160 of 262 staff, versus roughly 131 allowed. Firms were given 24 hours to respond or face proceedings under the CAQM Act 2021; Singh said monitoring would continue.
items.title: Gurugram Law Firms Cited for Breaching Work-From-Home Pollution Rule

items.summary: Three state-run oil marketing companies—Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum—rejected Karnataka's claim that petrol at some outlets contained ethanol above the 20% limit. The government said 11 of 14 samples from seven districts exceeded the threshold, with the highest concentration recorded in an IOCL sample. The OMCs disputed the sampling exercise conducted without their representatives and questioned whether certificates specified the required technical standards. They cited a joint quality-monitoring exercise testing all E20 samples within the prescribed range across 27 states and Union territories.
items.title: Karnataka OMCs Reject Ethanol Blending Claims

items.summary: A list of six new nonfiction books is set to be published in November, with all information sourced from the publishers. The selection spans biographies and memoirs: Paul Morley's David Hockney: An Artist for Life; Philip Delves Broughton's Embargo on how the 1973 oil crisis changed the world, more than 50 years later; Dan Jones's Castles: A Fortified History of the World; Ben Dark's Green Kingdom, tracing plant evolution from 484 million years ago through 16 families; Caitlin Moran's How to Be Hopeful; and Elena Dudum's Palestinian memoir They Told Me Back Home Would Be Beautiful.
items.title: Six New Nonfiction Titles for November

items.summary: A controversy has emerged in Karnataka over ethanol blending exceeding the mandated 20 percent limit, with fuel samples showing levels as high as 31.2 percent. Tests across seven districts, including Bengaluru, raised safety and vehicle concerns. Indian Oil Corporation Limited denied the claims, citing its own tests within regulated ranges. Major oil companies have proposed joint testing to ensure transparency.
items.title: Karnataka Raises Concerns Over Ethanol Blending Exceeding E20 Limits in Petrol

items.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh government released four protesters opposing the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project from Jully Central Jail near Itanagar on Saturday, nearly a month after their arrest. Detained on October 9 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, they were freed as a goodwill gesture toward the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum. The government said police cases would follow legal process and urged resumed talks with Chief Minister Pema Khandu, while withdrawal of security forces remains pending.
items.title: Arunachal Frees Siang Dam Protesters and Invites Return of Talks

items.summary: A Louisiana divorce dispute over shared property and spending tied to a new partner ended in an appellate reversal. The trial court ordered the wife to pay her former husband $205,000 for mishandling community assets. On appeal, the Third Circuit Court of Appeal rejected key parts of that ruling and instead ordered the husband to pay the wife $176,800. The article notes the reversal reflects errors in how the trial court classified, valued, or allocated property and spending, illustrating that Louisiana divorce judgments are not always final.
items.title: Louisiana Divorce Verdict Reversed on Appeal, Flipping Payment Direction

items.summary: Usman Khawaja has claimed that all members of the Australian cricket team, including support staff, were aware of sandpaper use during the 2018 South Africa tour. His account contradicts Cricket Australia's original investigation, which found only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft had prior knowledge. They received suspensions ranging from nine to 12 months. Both CA and former coach Darren Lehmann have rejected his allegations.
items.title: Khawaja claims entire Australian team knew of ball-tampering plan

items.summary: Police say a man lured an eight-year-old girl with golgappas, took her to an isolated plot about 500 metres from home, assaulted her and struck her on the head with an iron rod. Her body was recovered around 2am Saturday after it bore injury marks on the head. Police registered a case under sections 103(1) and 238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at Sikandrabad station, while teams trace the accused.
items.title: Bulandshahr Man Charged in Rape and Murder of Young Girl

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged a “deeply sinister plot” after Union minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh announced that voter ID cards, not Aadhaar, would determine eligibility for panchayati raj benefits. The announcement coincided with nationwide protests over an electoral-roll revision during which 13 crore electors were reportedly removed in affected states. Gandhi called the change a theft of rights and accused chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of colluding with the BJP to steal elections; Singh denied distorting facts, saying the shift prevents middlemen from exploiting schemes.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses BJP of Voter-Roll Manipulation and Aadhaar Shift

items.summary: An eight-year-old girl was allegedly raped and murdered on Friday after a man known to her family lured her out of her house under the pretext of treating her to golgappas. The accused, identified as Ravi Kashyap, reportedly took her about 500 metres from home, assaulted her and struck her with an iron rod before fleeing; her body was recovered around 2 am on Saturday. Police registered a case under Sections 103(1) and 238 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita at Sikandrabad police station.
items.title: Eight-Year-Old Girl Murdered in Bulandshahr After Being Lured by Known Man

items.summary: On the eve of Kali Puja, Bengalis observe Bhoot Chaturdashi by lighting fourteen earthen lamps and eating a dish called Choddo Shaak made from fourteen seasonal greens. The night marks remembering departed ancestors and protecting homes from wandering spirits, with popular belief linking it to fourteen generations remembered on this day. Food writer Amit Sen notes the occasion blurs the divide between living and departed people. MasterChef Oindrila Bala compares Bhoot Chaturdashi to Halloween, while food blogger Debjani Roy highlights the greens' health qualities. There is no fixed list of greens; households choose based on local produce and family preference, often avoiding onion and garlic.
items.title: Bengalis Eat Fourteen Seasonal Greens on Bhoot Chaturdashi

items.summary: The mythological film Ramayana has drawn praise for Yash's portrayal of Ravana, who many viewers and director Dolly call a show-stealer. The movie opened to strong response and collected Rs 180 crore at the box office. Producer Abhishek Agarwal instead highlighted Ranbir Kapoor's transformation as Lord Rama, while both he and director Nitesh Tiwari urged avoiding comparisons with Ramanand Sagar's classic Ramayan.
items.title: Yash Praised as Ramayana's Biggest Talking Point Over Ranbir Kapoor

items.summary: Hyderabad-based Minorities Welfare Minister Mohammad Azharuddin backed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's demand that he be allowed to speak in Parliament, saying discussions on the issue were welcome and noting Gandhi had long sought a debate. Azharuddin told ANI that while discussion could happen anywhere, parliamentary access was important. Separately, Union Minister Pralhad Joshi accused Gandhi of doing no homework on electoral roll revisions amid the row.
items.title: Minorities Minister Backs Congress Leader's Demand for Parliamentary Debate

items.summary: Actress Alia Bhatt shared pictures from her daughter Raha Kapoor's fourth birthday celebration on November 6. While the family moments drew attention, focus also turned to Alia's outfit: a floral Mirabel dress by Summer Away priced at Rs 8,720 per the brand's official website. Made of viscose georgette with a V-neckline and mini-length silhouette, it was styled understatedly for the event.
items.title: Alia Bhatt Wears ₹8,720 Floral Dress At Daughter Raha's Birthday

items.summary: Officials said on Saturday that Harry Boxer, a key operative of the wanted Lawrence Bishnoi gang, has been detained in the United States. American authorities apprehended him from California after inputs from Delhi Police's Special Cell and Haryana Police STF. He is linked to Rohit Shetty's February firing and other cases; Indian agencies are expected to seek his extradition with CBI assistance.
items.title: US Detains Lawrence Bishnoi Gang Operative Harry Boxer for Return to India

items.summary: Ahead of Diwali, Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration suspended 105 food business licences across the state during a special drive on November 4 and 5. The action included suspensions in Mumbai alone (28) and shutdown orders for outlets such as Rajdhani Biryani Centre. Suspected unsafe or adulterated stock worth over Rs 1.35 crore was seized from more than 69 establishments, despite prior warnings to vendors.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Licences of Quick-Commerce and Food-Franchise Firms Ahead of Diwali
